Which points were used

Requested: the last 40 points of the last two tests. Used: 36 points. When the last two tests (deney0_tur2_v2, 9 points; deney0_tekrar_testi, 41 points) are combined, all of the last 40 points fall in the repeat test. However, during the first ~4 minutes of this test the Motive rigid body was different: the pivot height changes from 0.71 m to 0.80 m, so the rigid body was re-created during the recording. The 5 points in that part have offsets of 34–48 cm, all in the same direction; this is a change of the reference, not a Marvelmind error. The first 300 s were therefore removed and the remaining 36 points analysed. For the same reason the two tests cannot be combined with one alignment (the combined fit gave 23 cm RMS).

Findings

1. Worse than run 1. The mean leave-one-out offset was 3.8 cm in run 1 and is 6.8 cm here; the alignment RMS went from 4.3 cm to 9.3 cm, and the point-to-point distance error from 4.4 cm to 7.2 cm RMS. This test covers a larger area (2.8 × 2.6 m) and three times as many points; the error may grow towards the edges of the area. The difference between the runs shows that the position-dependent Marvelmind error cannot be estimated from a single run.
2. The scale is still correct. Scale 1.006 over 630 point pairs (0.989 in run 1). No systematic stretching or shrinking; the error is scattered and position dependent.
3. One temporary wrong position. At point 19, 69 samples (~12 s) were more than 20 cm from the median. The analysis removed them. It is much smaller than the 2.3 m false lock on 6 November but may be the same kind of event.
4. The hedgehog mount offset came out at 18.8 cm (15.3 cm in run 1). Since the rigid body was re-created, the pivot changed too, so a different offset is expected. To keep runs comparable, the pivot should be placed on top of the hedgehog and not changed again.
5. The device clock drift is the same: 0.93 % (0.92 % in run 1). The drift is stable and can be corrected reliably in Experiment 1. The residual jitter in this recording is ~14 ms std.
6. Stops are short. Stops lasted 11–50 s (median 26 s); the plan asks for 60 s. This is enough for the jitter statistics, but 60 s would match the plan in the paper.

Next steps

  1. Define the rigid body once and keep it, with the pivot on top of the hedgehog. If it does not change between tests, runs can be combined with one alignment.
  2. Use 60 s stops; repeating the same points in two runs shows repeatability.
  3. To see where in the area the error concentrates, the points of run 1 and this test can be shown on one map (with separate alignments if the rigid body differs).
  4. Experiment 1 (latency).
